papers.abs: Polarization cavity solitons in coherently driven Kerr resonators undergo a sequence of dynamical bifurcations as the cavity detuning is increased. Here we show that a stationary localized state containing an Ising wall first becomes a fixed breather and then develops finite chirality and drift motion through a spontaneous non-equilibrium Ising-Bloch transition. Stability analyses identify the modes responsible for the breathing and the motion, revealing controllable dynamics of polarization cavity solitons.

papers.abs: Band topology and non-Hermitian spectral theory are now applied to mechanical metamaterials, chiral active fluids, stochastic networks, and open quantum systems. We give a tutorial synthesis organized by holonomy and by one question: what can the spectral data of a linear generator reveal about detailed balance? Three holonomies recur: the Berry phase of a band, the Burgers vector of a dislocation (the integrated torsion of the defect geometry), and the cycle affinity of a Markov network (the holonomy of the connection $\ln(W_{ij}/W_{ji})$). We rederive the Chern numbers $C_m=m(\mathrm{sgn}\,Ω+\mathrm{sgn}\,ν_o)$ of a compressible odd-viscous fluid and restate the dislocation zero-mode count of Paulose, Chen, and Vitelli as a pairing of integrated torsion with topological polarization. Our central message is that spectral topology can obstruct detailed balance but does not determine the magnitude of dissipation. papers.title: Optical frequency combs on thin-film lithium niobate: from principles to applications
papers.abs: Optical frequency combs, consisting of mutually coherent and equally spaced spectral lines, provide a powerful means of synthesizing, distributing, and processing optical frequencies on chip. Among integrated photonic platforms, thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is particularly attractive for comb generation because it combines strong electro-optic (EO) functionality, accessible $χ^{(2)}$ and $χ^{(3)}$ nonlinearities, low-loss nanophotonic confinement, and versatile dispersion engineering. This review summarizes the physical foundations and representative realizations of TFLN combs, and discusses their applications in optical communication, microwave photonics, optical computing, and precision metrology. The integration of nonlinear functionality, EO control, and passive photonic components is expected to advance compact, energy-efficient comb sources and broaden the utility of TFLN in integrated photonics and quantum optics.

papers.abs: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. papers.title: Off-focus detection for SNR enhancement in coherent single-pixel imaging
papers.abs: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. We show that appropriately selected off-focus Fourier-plane positions can improve reconstruction performance by suppressing fluctuation-sensitive coherent backgrounds while preserving spatially encoded signals. Experimentally, using a programmable liquid-crystal terahertz spatial light modulator and coherent heterodyne detection, we demonstrate improved amplitude and phase reconstruction from selected off-focus channels compared with focal detection. papers.title: X-ray parametric down-conversion probes radiation-induced dynamics in hybrid perovskite MAPbBr3
papers.abs: We report minute-timescale time-resolved measurements of X-ray parametric down-conversion (PDC) of X-rays into ultraviolet photons in a MAPbBr3 single crystal under continuous irradiation. Despite the known radiation sensitivity of hybrid perovskites and the high photon flux required to detect the intrinsically weak PDC signal, the nonlinear response remains measurable throughout the irradiation sequence. Both PDC and Bragg diffraction exhibit a slow decay consistent with diffusion-driven damage dynamics on timescales reported for bromide-vacancy and proton migration. However, despite their similar decay rates, the PDC and Bragg signals evolve toward markedly different steady states, while an additional fast decay component is observed in the Bragg response but absent in the PDC signal. Density functional theory calculations identify N 2s states of the methylammonium cation as the most likely contributors to the measured PDC response and show that their Fourier component is only weakly affected by bromide-vacancy formation. papers.abs: Near-perfect light absorption in ultrathin films is hindered by two fundamental obstacles: the momentum mismatch that prevents resonant excitation of surface exciton-polaritons (SEPs) under ordinary illumination, and the 50% absorption ceiling imposed on free-standing conductive sheets by geometric symmetry. Here we show that both obstacles can be overcome simultaneously in a simple, planar geometry. A one-dimensional periodic grating of anisotropic polarizable ribbons composed of J-aggregates supporting bright molecular excitons provides the reciprocal lattice momentum needed to excite SEPs without employing an attenuated total reflection configuration, while a metallic mirror beneath a dielectric spacer folds the reflected field back onto the absorber, breaking the $50\%$ limit through interference between the incident and reflected waves. papers.title: Plasmon excitations in monolayer stanene
papers.abs: Monolayer stanene exhibits strong intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and notably distinct low-energy band features involving both $Γ$ and K valleys together with strong electron-hole asymmetry among group-IV monolayers. Its plasmonic properties and external-field tunability remain largely unclarified. Here, we systematically investigate its high-energy plasmon structures and low-energy collective excitation modulated by temperature, electrostatic doping and perpendicular electric field. Calculations use a $sp^3$ tight-binding model with SOC and sublattice staggered potentials, combined with the finite-temperature multiband Lindhard function under the random-phase approximation. Besides the $π$ and $π+σ$ plasmon known in graphene/silicene, stanene supports two new high-energy plasmon branches. papers.abs: Photonic processors are emerging as promising platforms in the race towards the realization of practical universal quantum computers. Several architectures with universal capabilities have been proposed for their implementation via a photonic platform, each with their own set of benefits and drawbacks. The proposed architecture is modular, allowing for a high degree of flexibility and scalability, and relies on a loop-based structure, significantly reducing the number of physical components required to implement it experimentally. We prove that our architecture is universal, deterministic, and compatible with the quantum circuital model, as well as reprogrammable and capable of adaptive measurements. papers.title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
papers.abs: Background: Diagnostic I-131 whole-body planar imaging in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is count-limited by low administered activity, and quality worsens under rapid acquisition. Models trained on such data struggle because their targets lack photon statistics. Purpose: To test whether high-quality post-therapeutic (PT) I-131 scans can serve as superior training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images, using transfer learning and input-image addition. Methods: In this single-center prospective study, 111 patients were enrolled in PT training (n = 19), diagnostic follow-up (FU) training (n = 58), and FU paired test (n = 34) cohorts. Five Restormer-based models were trained: FU_DLx2 on FU labels; PT_DLx2 transfer-learned on PT data; PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ with input-image addition; PT_DLx6 as a PT-only reference. Test-time processing used two-step denormalization and Poisson re-scaling to preserve noise statistics. papers.title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
papers.abs: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2~mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450~mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured $S_{21}$ at 2.45 GHz was $-$18.8~dB, versus $-$60.9~dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint $\pm$5~mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE~802.11n test demonstrated a 65~Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at $-$20~dBm transmit power through the coupler link. papers.title: Long-distance quantum secure direct communication with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits
papers.abs: The Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) code possesses a lattice periodic structure that enables the effective correction of small displacement errors induced by noise in phase space, which is indispensable for quantum computation. The GKP code was also used to construct a long-distance entanglement channel in quantum repeaters and distribute random keys in quantum key distribution (QKD). Using GKP encoding, we propose a quantum secure direct communication (QSDC) protocol that not only transmits the secret message directly, but also helps protect the safety of communication personnel. The exponential attenuation loss of photons can be overcome by the third-generation quantum repeater. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that secure transmission distance exceeding 1000 km is achievable with a 23 dB squeezing level. Furthermore, we establish a cost-based optimization framework to characterize the trade-off among secure communication distance, secrecy capacity, and repeater resources, enabling optimized repeater deployment and providing a systematic design strategy for scalable quantum

papers.title: Lensless single-pixel imaging through dynamic coded-aperture illumination
papers.abs: We demonstrate a lensless single-pixel imaging (SPI) system combining dynamic coded-aperture illumination with single-pixel detection. Binary digital micromirror device (DMD) masks generate tailored grayscale intensity fields through coherent propagation, without relay projection optics or temporal grayscale synthesis. Six target-field configurations---uniform, Rayleigh speckle, squared-Rayleigh speckle, and sparse binary fields with $p=10\%$, $5\%$, and $1\%$---are evaluated using binary and grayscale objects. Intensity-correlation and nonnegative total-variation-regularized reconstructions reveal that the preferred illumination depends on the object, reconstruction method, and evaluation metric. By combining rapid binary modulation, programmable grayscale illumination, and single-pixel readout, this implementation provides a flexible architecture for lensless computational imaging and joint design of optical encoding and reconstruction.

papers.title: Origin of devil's staircases and anomalous Arnold tongues of breathing solitons in optical Kerr resonators
papers.abs: Synchronization phenomena are ubiquitous across natural and engineered systems, and optical resonators supporting breathing solitons offer a natural platform for their investigation. In driven Kerr cavities described by the Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE), breathing-soliton dynamics constitute a minimal setting in which such behavior can be systematically analyzed. Despite recent observations of intricate self-synchronization structures in mode-locked lasers-such as subharmonic entrainment, devil's staircases, and holes within Arnold tongues, i.e., regions of unsynchronized dynamics embedded within synchronized domains-their physical origin has remained elusive due to the complexity of laser dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that these phenomena emerge in the universal framework of the LLE. By reducing the problem to this model, we uncover the mechanism responsible for both the devil's staircase and the formation of holes within Arnold tongues. papers.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
papers.abs: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. papers.title: Super-resolution quantum imaging via multiphoton correlation
papers.abs: The resolution of conventional imaging is fundamentally constrained by the diffraction limit. Here we demonstrate that this limit can be overcome using classical thermal light, through the correlation of multiphoton subsystems. By resolving the photon numbers detected in the two arms of a Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer, the correlation function exhibits a narrowed peak or dip whose width is tunable via the average photon number. Temporal and spatial super-resolution enhancements up to 11.8-fold and 5.1-fold, respectively, are experimentally achieved. As a proof-of-principle experiment, a double-pinhole that is completely unresolved by standard ghost imaging becomes clearly distinguishable via the correlation of two-photon versus zero-photon. The principle of this super-resolution imaging can be interpreted as a combination of classical super-resolution imaging and quantum super-resolution imaging. This work provides a versatile platform for super-resolution imaging and lithography, and opens a new avenue for exploring the boundary between classical and nonclassical phenomena.

papers.title: Advantage Distillation in Paired-State Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abs: We investigate advantage distillation for paired-state Loop-Back quantum key distribution, with a fixed optical station serving a lightweight portable terminal. Alice prepares two polarization-encoded pulses, Bob selects and applies a polarization filter to each pulse, and Alice infers his selections from the returned detection pattern. The proposed advantage-distillation step selects consistent blocks of three two-bit records using two independent public parity checks on a minimal connected graph. The closing edge of a parity polygon is shown to be redundant: any spanning tree of the same vertices has the same acceptance set. We derive exact acceptance probabilities, residual-error laws, and retention rates. Under independent bit errors, the three-record filter reduces the leading error term from e to e^2, while its cost in discarded records and public information is accounted for explicitly. papers.title: Wavelength-resolved polarization characterization of supercontinuum vector beams
papers.abs: The polarization state of a supercontinuum (SC) vector beam provides a reference for quantitative polarimetry. We characterize an azimuthally polarized SC vector beam generated with an S-waveplate and azimuthal polarizers by wavelength-resolved Stokes imaging. Representative maps show an approximately tangential azimuthal angle and a small ellipticity parameter over much of the beam, together with the degree of polarization. The {\pm} 90° azimuthal angle boundary shifts by about 21° between 450 and 766 nm. A linear fit gives 21° {\pm} 7°, where the uncertainty is derived from the slope confidence interval and does not include uncharacterized systematic errors. Jones-matrix calculations examine candidate imperfections under specified assumptions. Attributing the measured boundary shift to this mechanism requires an intensity extinction ratio of about 7 or less at 766 nm if the offset at 450 nm is negligible and the shift corresponds to a uniform azimuthal angle change. papers.title: Coherent Control of High-Order Lightwave Currents in Gate-Tunable Bilayer Graphene
papers.abs: The sub-cycle acceleration of charge carriers in an electronic circuit by tailored terahertz (THz) electric-field waveforms, rather than conventional pulsed bias voltages, opens a transformative frontier for lightwave electronics operating far beyond the scaling limits of gigahertz electronic technologies. Yet gate-tunable coherent control of multi-order and non-perturbative currents has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate lightwave control over the amplitude, phase flips, and zero-crossings of THz field-driven high-order currents by utilizing phase-locked pairs of single-cycle THz fields in a dual-gated bilayer graphene (BLG) device. By leveraging the in-situ tuning of both bandgap and charge doping, we reveal extreme THz photocurrent rectification and sub-THz-cycle current generation that are governed by a strong field-driven crossover from interband multi-photon coherence to intraband lightwave acceleration, whose competition provides an exceptional sensitivity to the THz-pulse pair drive. papers.abs: This comment addresses the publication [Appl. Opt. 65, 7090 (2026)] which targets an alleged ``optimization'' of a patented invention conceived by the author. The invention had introduced a multi-temperature management scheme for a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity that optimized the crystal temperature around the beam waist for phase-matching, while utilizing independently adjustable temperatures in other regions of the same crystal to simultaneously satisfy the double-resonance condition. A foundational form of this invention was initially utilized by co-author H. Vahlbruch without the author's prior knowledge during the construction of the squeezed-light laser for the Virgo gravitational wave detector. In their publication, the three authors now propose a variant that reduces the maximum achievable temperature differential. papers.title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
papers.abs: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 φ)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer Rényi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. papers.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
papers.abs: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical models, and a framework for future investigations on this material.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Maximally Entangled OAM States by Joint Pump and Modal-Space Engineering
papers.abs: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) generates correlated photon pairs that inherently exhibit high-dimensional spatial entanglement in orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes. In practice, the resulting two-photon states are typically not maximally entangled due to a highly non-uniform distribution of generated OAM modes. Although pump-beam engineering has emerged as a tool to prepare high-dimensional entangled states, it has usually been restricted to low-dimensional subspaces, i.e., small sets of selected OAM modes for each photon within the full infinite-dimensional two-photon Hilbert space. A general understanding of the requirements for the generation of maximally entangled states (MESs) for any dimensionality $d$ with $d>2$ is lacking. Here, we demonstrate how pump engineering enables the generation of high-dimensional MESs for arbitrary $d$ defined in $d \times d$ subspaces. papers.title: Collective Chiral Response of Achiral Plasmonic Arrays Induced by Truncated Bloch-Floquet Effect
papers.abs: Chirality in plasmonic systems is commonly associated with structures differentiated by their handedness. Here, we demonstrate the emergence of collective chirality in structurally achiral periodic hole arrays induced by non-local surface-plasmon interactions. We attribute this effect to the transfer of the optical angular momentum in the system. While an individual sub-wavelength circular aperture is not expected to alter the total angular momentum, the periodic structure results in a coherent coupling of plasmons wavefronts, giving rise to a collective Bloch-Floquet-like response. The edge of the structure accumulates the helical phase that eventually results in a visible spin-dependent shifting of the plasmonic beam. We systematically study the effects of hole-array size, periodicity and the geometry. The observed phenomenon shows an unprecedented robustness and consistency. papers.title: Coherent Conversion of an Interacting Dark-State-Polariton Condensate into a Photonic Bose-Einstein Condensate
papers.abs: An interacting condensate can retain an observable imprint of its preparation after the interactions are switched off. For light, accessing this regime requires separating the formation of a photon condensate from the material medium that redistributes its energy. We investigate a multimode-cavity scheme in which an interacting dark-state-polariton condensate is coherently converted into a confined photonic Bose-Einstein condensate as the atom-cavity coupling is removed. The polariton mass, matter fraction, and particle number control the condensate occupation during preparation. Remarkably, changing the mass also modifies the condensate's response to repulsion through the spatial overlap of its orbitals, even when the entire single-particle spectrum is held fixed. Ideal mode-preserving conversion conserves the full natural-orbital occupation spectrum, while finite-time few-body calculations show that additional occupation changes during transfer are much smaller than those established during interacting preparation. papers.title: Adaptive Quantum Metrology of Gravitational Waves
papers.abs: We develop a feedback-controlled quantum metrology scheme to probe weak gravitational waves (GWs) through their direct energy exchange with light. Adaptive SU(2) direction control, based on current estimates of the GW frequency and phase, allows the frequency shifts acquired in successive interaction intervals to add rather than cancel. The resulting persistent frequency difference is converted into an optical phase difference for interferometric readout. We further extend the scheme to elliptically polarized GWs using two transverse sensing channels separated by $45^\circ$ to probe the $+$ and $\times$ components independently. After the GW interaction, the two signals are mapped onto orthogonal polarization modes, enabling phase accumulation along a common path. We derive the corresponding quantum Fisher information matrix and find a $T_{\rm int}^2T_{\rm ph}^2$ scaling in the ideal coherent regime. For a fixed-photon-number probe, the sensitivity shows Heisenberg-like $1/n$ scaling in the ideal case.

A first-order purity map connects the reachable delay ratio and bandwidth--length product to the photon-pair spectrum. A full-vector AlN/TiO$_2$ feasibility example satisfies direct phase matching with a ratio of pump--idler to pump--signal group-delay mismatches of $-0.899$ and yields a calculated unfiltered Schmidt purity of 0.789 over 5 mm. papers.abs: Clifford and Clifford's algorithm samples single-photon boson sampling exactly, one output mode at a time, by adding the input photons in a uniformly random order. papers.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
papers.abs: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. We discuss strategies to improve photon indistinguishability, including radiative-rate engineering, charge stabilization, and more selective excitation. papers.title: Bias-free superconducting microwave nonreciprocity from a passive nonlinear resonator
papers.abs: Routing microwave tones in a nonreciprocal fashion in a superconducting chip usually requires an external bias, commonly in the form of static magnetic fields, pump tones or temporal modulation. Here we demonstrate microwave nonreciprocity in a bias-free, passive platform, a single nonlinear superconducting resonator patterned in one film without Josephson junctions. Unequal coupling with the two feeding ports makes its nonlinear resonance shift direction-dependent, and its sharp Fano lineshape converts this asymmetric response into a large transmission contrast when excited from opposite directions. Our niobium nitride (NbN) device reaches a directional contrast of 53.0 dB at an insertion loss of 4.6 dB, and it exceeds 20 dB over 9.7 MHz. Time-resolved measurements show that the device routes pulses from 2 us to 1 ms with more than 30 dB of contrast and switches within a few microseconds. Made with the same technology as superconducting amplifiers, such bias-free nonreciprocal components could simplify the on-chip routing of strong pump and control tones in quantum processors

papers.abs: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. papers.abs: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as an extraordinary platform for polaritonics, given their remarkable ability to confine light to deep sub-wavelength scales. However, as material thicknesses reach the nanometer limit, macroscopic electrodynamic models become inadequate for the description of light-matter coupling in 2D materials, leaving a significant gap in our understanding of 2D polaritons. In this work, we develop a comprehensive quantum microscopic framework that describes 2D polaritons through a general, scale-less Hamiltonian. Starting from the quantum properties of a polarizable 2D surface, we derive collective excitations and we identify both transverse electric magnetic modes existing outside the light cone. Our results demonstrate that these 2D systems facilitate a powerful synergy between extreme wavelength shrinking and intrinsic quantum squeezing of electric field quadratures. papers.title: Nonlinear Optical Properties of MXenes for Photonic Applications
papers.abs: MXenes - a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides - have emerged as powerful nonlinear photonic materials owing to their metallic conductivity, ultrafast carrier dynamics, broadband optical response, and highly tunable surface chemistry. This Review provides the first comprehensive overview of the nonlinear optical (NLO) properties of MXenes and their growing impact on advanced photonic technologies. We discuss state-of-the-art synthesis strategies, from fluoride-based etching to molten-salt, electrochemical, and CVD-enabled routes, highlighting how structural quality and surface terminations govern optical behaviour. A detailed analysis of third-order nonlinearities including Kerr effects, two- and multi-photon absorption, saturable and reverse-saturable absorption, and harmonic generation is presented, supported by quantitative comparisons across MXene families. papers.title: From Machine-Discovered Graphs to Analytic NOON State Families
papers.abs: Machine-discovered graphs generate NOON states after heralding and output-number selection, but their interference mechanisms and optical implementations are not immediately apparent. We derive analytic weight conditions for arbitrary photon number $N$ by counting pair-generation processes that cancel mixed output occupations. These conditions yield quantum experiments by path identity using a Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer and photon-pair sources. Takagi decomposition of the pair-amplitude matrix gives an exact Gaussian implementation using single-mode squeezers followed by a passive interferometer. Any pure, zero-displacement Gaussian scheme with photon-number-resolved heralding requires at least $N-2$ herald photons, and both constructions attain this bound. At finite gain, the ideal Takagi implementation maintains unit fidelity after output-number selection, whereas fidelity decreases in path identity with fixed source settings.

papers.title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain
papers.abs: Thouless pumping provides a powerful route for probing Chern topology through quantized motion in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate such a topological pump in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. A graphical representation in Bloch space is used to construct pumping schemes. In this framework, the Bloch vector traces a closed loop that evolves in time. The Chern number of the synthetic band is then determined by the motion of this loop. Quantum pumping phenomena are demonstrated for a filled band and for a bosonic wave packet driven by Bloch oscillations. We further show that the Haldane model can be mapped to the driven extended SSH chain by replacing a quasimomentum by the pumping time. The quantized charge pump indicates that the Chern number of a two-dimensional model can be read out from a one-dimensional pumping protocol, offering an accessible route for detecting higher-dimensional topology, such as in photonic and cold-atom platforms.

papers.abs: We develop a dynamical model of squeezed-state generation in nonlinear optical microresonators that takes into account the back-action of the signal mode on the pump mode. The dynamical approach is extended to a three-mode Kerr microresonator with two pump modes. Separately, we investigate stationary squeezing in a reduced five-mode model with fixed pump amplitudes, including a parasitic single-pump spontaneous four-wave-mixing channel. papers.title: Intensity limits for phase-only holographic optical-tweezer arrays
papers.abs: Optical tweezers use tightly focused laser beams to trap and manipulate individual particles, enabling advances in quantum computing, drug discovery, and biological research. Scaling these technologies to large arrays requires delivering sufficient light to every trapping site while minimizing the total laser power required. Here, we investigate the fundamental limits of how efficiently a phase-only hologram can distribute light across an array of optical traps. We derive upper bounds on the minimum intensity across trapping sites, accounting for illumination, target geometry, and diffraction from spatial light modulator pixels. For arrays arranged in a single plane or across two axial planes, we show how these limits scale with the number of traps and SLM pixels, and establish conditions for focusing light in three dimensions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that optimized holograms can closely approach these theoretical limits, suggesting that further improvements in phase optimization alone offer limited power savings. papers.title: Dynamical Light-Matter Coupling with Protected Superconducting Oscillators
papers.abs: Superconducting circuits hosting long-lived bosonic modes are an excellent platform for emulating the dynamics of light and matter and exploiting them for quantum information processing. The space of accessible dynamics is greatly extended by introducing the frequency tunability of artificial atoms, whereby the interactions with the light field of a microwave cavity can be modified on demand. However, using external flux bias to control the frequency of transmons introduces significant losses to coupled cavities, reducing their single-photon lifetimes to a few tens of $μ$s. These imperfections compromise the usefulness of the bosonic mode, which loses its ability to store and manipulate the quantum information of many-photon states. This thesis investigates the issue and demonstrates how to enhance the flux control of microwave cavities without compromising protection. Several hardware solutions were explored, including off-plane remote flux sources routed by a magnetic hose, and lithographically printed on-chip lines equipped with multiple stages of filtering. papers.title: Adaptive wavefront shaping through flexible multicore photonic lantern fibres
papers.abs: Holographic micro-endoscopy enables images to be funnelled all-optically through hair-thin strands of optical fibre. Future applications of this technology encompass biomedical imaging within mobile organisms, LiDAR, and industrial inspection. Yet holographic imaging through dynamically flexible optical fibres, called for in many real-world scenarios, represents an ongoing challenge. In this work we demonstrate how a bespoke fibre architecture that we term a 'photonic lantern fibre' offers a way forward. This device benefits from the negligible modal cross-talk of a polarisation-maintaining multicore fibre throughout the majority of its length. A tapered region at one end - known as a photonic lantern - guides light to a short segment of multimode optical fibre. We show how this fibre enables the projection of high-fidelity structured light to the multimode distal fibre facet via wavefront shaping, providing a level of optical control beyond that possible using conventional multicore fibres which suffer from aliasing due to their spatially separated cores. papers.title: Experimental visual quantum state discrimination
papers.abs: Almost all solutions to vision tasks $\unicode{x2014}$ offered by nature and technology alike $\unicode{x2014}$ rely on capturing an image using a lens or a similar optical instrument, followed by computational analysis by neurons of a brain or a digital computer. This approach is inherently suboptimal in photon-limited and noisy conditions, where critical information is irreversibly lost at the measurement stage. We address this gap by introducing AI-driven optimization of quantum measurements on the incoming photons, learning how to extract the maximum possible information for a given computer vision task from each incoming photon. The trained measurement consists of a diffractive optical neural network (DONN) followed by a detector array. We train the DONN with a quantum information-theoretic objective that maximizes the rate at which the discrimination error decays as photons accumulate. papers.abs: Understanding magnetization dynamics in metallic van der Waals ferromagnets is essential to uncover their magnetic interactions and evaluate their potential for high-frequency spintronics applications. At high temperatures, the FMR response is dominated by a single broad resonance that shifts toward lower magnetic fields upon cooling. papers.title: Symplectic Reck: In-Situ Learning of Gaussian Quantum Operations
papers.abs: Programmable photonic circuits are a natural platform for physical learning, where hardware parameters are trained directly from measured feedback. We propose a physical learning algorithm and architecture for continuous-variable quantum systems where a photonic circuit is trained in situ to invert an unknown lossless Gaussian quantum operation. We prove that a generic symplectic matrix $S\in\mathrm{Sp}(2N,\mathbb{R})$ admits a decomposition into a triangular array of two-mode symplectic gates on neighboring modes, followed by single-mode symplectic gates. We then introduce the symplectic Reck mesh, which physically realizes this factorization, generalizing the unitary Reck mesh widely used in optical neural networks. When placed after an unknown Gaussian unitary, the mesh is trained in situ by nulling local response blocks one at a time using optical probes and measurements. We identify a local condition number that quantifies the squeezing required for a nulling step and its sensitivity to measurement error. papers.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
papers.abs: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. From this single picture we obtain the blue of the sky and the white of the clouds, transparency and the refractive index, the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem, reflection and the colours of thin films, why metals reflect and what gives metals and semiconductors their colours, polarizers, Brewster's angle and birefringence, the working of mirrors, lenses, microscopes and the eye, the propagation of a few-cycle pulse through a slab, Cherenkov radiation, amplification and second-harmonic generation. papers.abs: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. At 1550 nm, the device exhibits rise and fall times of 17.7 and 40.2 s, respectively, and an estimated shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 1.3 * 10^6 Jones. papers.abs: Infrared spectroscopy is a key tool to study complex structural dynamics in molecular systems. However, resolving weak or broad vibrational modes is challenging due to their rapid decay. Here, we demonstrate a technique to significantly extend the detectable lifetime - and thereby spectral resolution - of molecular signatures by employing synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. Utilizing a Cr:ZnS laser system and a nonlinear ZnGeP2 crystal, we achieve a 10-fold increase in the electric field strength of the infrared molecular signal, yielding a two-orders of magnitude enhancement in dynamic range and a 2-fold increase in the signal-to-noise ratio. Using isopropyl alcohol as a model system, we demonstrate that OPA-enhanced detection extends the observable window of vibrational modes up to 72 %. papers.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
papers.abs: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

papers.title: Witnessing Polarization Entanglement of Annihilation Photons via Compton Scattering
papers.abs: Experimentally certifying polarization entanglement in annihilation photons is challenging because polarizers are unavailable in the high-energy regime and one needs to rely on Compton polarimetry. Previously proposed schemes designed for this task are either experimentally unfeasible or require a specific source state model. We address these issues by reformulating Compton scattering as a continuous-outcome quantum instrument, thereby enabling the prediction of the scattering angles and the post-scattering polarization state. Our framework allows connecting Compton polarimetry with entanglement witnesses by deriving experimentally accessible lower bounds on Bell state fidelities for arbitrary initial two-photon polarization states. We discuss how this witness can be extracted from coarse-grained coincidence measurements with detectors of almost any angular resolution. The presented scheme does not require knowledge of angle-independent empirical factors like detector efficiencies and source activity. papers.abs: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. papers.title: Cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation from Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O
papers.abs: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity. These results establish cavity-enhanced SHG spectroscopy as a valuable tool for studying Rydberg excitons in microcavities and provide a pathway towards exploiting optical nonlinearities in Rydberg exciton polariton systems.

papers.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
papers.abs: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.

papers.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
papers.abs: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical estimations indicate that effective symmetry breaking in the tetralayer heterostructure is driven by interlayer hybridization, giving rise to pronounced electronic and phononic signatures. A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
papers.abs: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.

papers.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
papers.abs: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.

papers.abs: Engineering of two-dimensional material heterostructures offers a broad range of degrees of freedom through the selection of type and number of layers and their relative stacking configurations. In these compound materials, the stacking sequence plays a central role in determining electronic, mechanical, and optical properties. Here, we present a theoretical study of its signature on the excitons of hexagonal boron nitride bilayers based on first-principle calculations within the GW approximation and the Bethe-Salpeter equation. We explain how stacking-dependent symmetry variations lead to distinct electronic structures, particularly near the band edge around the K high-symmetry point, and consequently to markedly different excitonic landscapes. Indeed, we analyze the symmetry-governed character of the low-lying excitonic states, identifying their bright or dark nature for each stacking configuration and performing a systematic comparison. papers.title: Interface-driven second harmonic generation in indium tin oxide/gold nanolayers: density and mass discontinuities matter
papers.abs: Second harmonic generation from transparent conductive oxides and metals is traditionally attributed to Coulomb, magnetic Lorentz, and convective sources. We show that this picture is incomplete in deeply subwavelength indium tin oxide/gold bilayers. Measurements reveal two robust spectral features, a broad maximum near 1000 nm and an epsilon-near-zero peak near 1350 nm, that persist across wide variations in material and excitation parameters. Hydrodynamic-Maxwell simulations identify an interface-specific convective mechanism activated by freeelectron density and effective-mass discontinuities at the oxide-metal boundary. As electronic homogenization develops across the bilayer, the response evolves toward one described by conventional Coulomb, Lorentz, and leading convective terms. These results establish second harmonic generation as a sensitive probe of interface-driven nonlinearities and suggest a broader role for electronic discontinuities in shaping nonlinear optical processes at surface and buried material interfaces.

papers.title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
papers.abs: Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. That is not necessarily the case in the quantum regime, where this kind of behavior around EPs, to a large extent, remains elusive. In fact, the interplay between dissipation and quantum fluctuations makes the complete Lindbladian evolution quite different from effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian descriptions. In this context, we investigate the signatures of the Liouvillian EPs on spectral and dynamic response by considering properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances. Even though our approach is generic, we focus on two paradigmatic models-a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system, where we investigate the role of quantum jumps and interactions in the Liouvillian spectrum, in terms of complex and structured pseudospectra. papers.title: Exceptional Topological Bound States in the Continuum
papers.abs: Topological phases, exceptional points, and bound states in the continuum (BICs) are three key concepts in condensed matter and classical wave physics. Their pairwise combinations have yielded a rich variety of intriguing singular modes, but the triple merger--exceptional topological BICs (ET-BICs)--has yet to be explored. In this Letter, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a universal approach for constructing such elusive exceptional structures. The system consists of four coupled topological chains: y-mirror stacking generates pairs of topological BICs, while z-stacking with biased loss yields a generalized mirror symmetry under which each pair--separated in different subspaces until their collapse--merges into an ET-BIC at a critical loss. Experimentally, using an acoustic platform with electrically tunable loss, we not only directly observe the coalescence of eigenenergies but also the coalescence of eigenstates, offering a complete verification of the ET-BIC formation. papers.abs: High-intensity terahertz (THz) sources combining high repetition rates, strong field amplitudes, and long-term stability are key enabling technologies for next-generation ultrafast photonics. As a proof of concept, the source was integrated into an atom probe tomography (APT) instrument. papers.abs: BaMgF4 (BMF) has the potential to serve as a platform material for vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) nonlinear optics owing to its ferroelectricity and high UV transparency down to 130 nm. However, the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients reported for BMF span approximately one order of magnitude, hindering a reliable assessment of its potential for nonlinear optical applications. Here, we redetermined these coefficients by combining Maker fringe, wedge, and single-pass second-harmonic-generation measurements at a fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm. Our results establish that all the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BMF lie in the range of 0.01-0.04 pm/V. We determined d31 to be 0.035 pm/V, which is among the largest coefficients of BMF, while it has been underestimated relative to the other coefficients in previous studies. Although d31 is not the largest coefficient, the use of its long corresponding coherence length is beneficial for quasi-phase matching, particularly for VUV generation, where the fabrication of lower-order quasi-phase-matching structures is crucial.

papers.title: When is an Optical Design Problem a Mass Transfer Problem?
papers.abs: This paper investigates whether optical design problems can be represented as Monge--Kantorovich mass transfer problems with some cost function. A necessary condition for such equivalence is derived in the semi-discrete setting. It allows a transport representation to be ruled out without choosing a cost function in advance. The condition is applied to the near-field refractor problem and to the design of two refracting surfaces transforming a spherical beam into a spherical or collimated beam. papers.title: Pressure-induced symmetry breaking and polarity in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr
papers.abs: The van der Waals magnet CrSBr has emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring coupled structural, magnetic, and electronic phenomena. Yet, the evolution of its crystal symmetry and electronic states under pressure and temperature remains unresolved. To elucidate this we employ low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman scattering and photoluminescence measurements under hydrostatic pressures of up to 12 GPa, complemented by first-principles calculations.We observe a cascade of pressure-induced structural transitions from the orthorhombic $Pmmn$ to monoclinic $P2_1/m$ phase at $\approx$ 1.5 GPa, followed by the emergence of a polar orthorhombic $Pmm$2 phase $\approx$ 6.5 GPa. The change in symmetry is accompanied by phonon anomalies and a direct-to-indirect bandgap crossover. Our results demonstrate pressure as a knob to engineer structure, symmetry and electronic properties in CrSBr in a coupled manner.

papers.abs: Recent experimental demonstrations of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) have attracted significant attention for their ability to establish information-theoretically secure encryption keys for next-generation communication systems. As practical deployment accelerates, the realization of compact, scalable, and high-throughput discrete-variable (DV) QKD systems has become increasingly important. While advances in photonic integration are enabling low-size, low-weight, and low-power QKD hardware, the security and performance of these systems rely heavily on efficient post-processing techniques to generate identical, secure keys. This tutorial presents a comprehensive algorithm-level review of practical post-processing techniques for DV-QKD, with particular emphasis on information reconciliation methods based on Cascade, Winnow, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and polar codes. papers.title: Low-Rank Iteration for Efficient Calculations of Topological Surface States
papers.abs: Surface states are hallmarks of topological phases, and their efficient computation is crucial for topology characterization. Conventional supercell methods (SCM) approximate semi-infinite systems as finite periodic ones, but suffer from high computational cost, artificial inter-surface coupling, and slow convergence near band edges. Recently, boundary problems for semi-infinite systems have been recast as block-tridiagonal equations and solved by the cyclic reduction method (CRM) and the transfer matrix method (TMM). However, these approaches remain resource-intensive, as fine-mesh discretization produces very large matrices. papers.abs: We study single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain, comparing a full microscopic model with an independent-radiation approximation. For a reference chain, a decomposition into collective atomic resonances relates this discrepancy mainly to spectral-phase changes caused by the omitted interatomic couplings. Parameter scans delimit this phase-dominated regime, and controlled comparisons separate the effects of coherent exchange and collective decay.

papers.abs: Histopathology, the microscopic examination of stained tissue sections, remains the gold standard for pathology imaging, but its bright-field imaging is largely morphological. papers.title: Time- and phase-resolved emulation of sign-selective counterdiabatic dynamics in a superconducting qutrit
papers.abs: In cyclic three-level systems, phase-sensitive interference can convert a coupling-sign reversal into a population contrast, providing a controllable analogue of handedness. We emulate this mechanism in a superconducting transmon qutrit using two resonant single-photon drives and a phase-controlled effective two-photon drive. Effective loop phases \(Φ_L=+π/2\) and \(Φ_R=-π/2\), separated by \(π\), reverse the auxiliary contribution to the dark--bright coupling, canceling the intrinsic nonadiabatic term for \(L\) and reinforcing it for \(R\). Time-resolved trajectories reveal dark-pathway transfer for \(L\) and bright-manifold participation for \(R\). Measured late-time averages give a target-state population contrast of 0.929. Loop-phase measurements establish phase selectivity, while pulse-area and common-mode amplitude scans characterize the operating regime and control sensitivity. These results provide direct time- and phase-domain access to sign-selective counterdiabatic interference in a programmable cyclic qutrit.

papers.abs: We numerically investigate dissipative dark-soliton (DDS) microcombs under the action of pure high even-order normal (HEON) dispersion in a microresonator with the self-injection locking (SIL). Pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion can support DDSs formed by interlocked switching waves, directly excited through a SIL-based turnkey scheme without detuning sweeps. Compared to the pure 4th-order case, the switching-wave tail oscillation period increases and its decay rate decreases with the increase of the dispersion order. Although the overall comb bandwidth narrows, the number of non-pump comb lines above a common absolute power threshold increases. Furthermore, the feedback phase controls the DDS duty cycle and intracavity comb-line power distribution, while the increase of the pump power improves the estimated pump-to-comb output conversion efficiency.

papers.title: Growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb quantum devices
papers.abs: We report recent progress in the growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb Majorana devices for three-terminal correlation experiments. A critical prerequisite for these devices is a continuous Pb film spanning from the PbTe nanowire to the substrate. In previous studies, PbTe nanowires were spatially separated from the substrate mask, making them unable to fulfill this requirement. To address this issue, we have developed a new growth and fabrication approach. Key fabrication steps are introduced between the PbTe growth and Pb deposition. The top facet of the PbTe nanowire is covered with a Te capping layer before breaking the ultra-high vacuum, enabling ex situ processing for subsequent steps. The mask is then removed, followed by the fabrication of shadow walls. After reloading the chip into the growth chamber, the Te protection layer is removed through thermal decomposition, and the Pb film is subsequently deposited. papers.title: Differential chiral sensing at exceptional points in intrinsically chiral metastructures
papers.abs: Discriminating opposite enantiomers through their weak chiroptical responses remains a fundamental challenge in optical sensing. Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian singularities at which eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, offer a route to enhanced spectral responses through their characteristic square-root eigenvalue splitting. However, their potential for chiral discrimination remains largely unexplored. We demonstrate exceptional points in an intrinsically chiral hybrid metamaterial and reveal strongly asymmetric responses to enantiomeric perturbations. The interplay between intrinsic chirality and non-Hermitian degeneracy is realized through the coupling of a chiral plasmonic nanoantenna array to a photonic crystal slab. We observe characteristic complex-square-root scaling, with both resonance frequencies and loss-rates exhibiting pronounced handedness dependence. Remarkably, opposite enantiomers produce complex mode splittings that differ by more than an order of magnitude. Our findings establish intrinsic chirality as a new degree of freedom in non-Hermitian physics an

papers.title: Laser-Direct-Written polymer WGM microring laser integrated on a fiber tip for refractive index sensing
papers.abs: Whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microlasers are promising for refractometric sensing, but their practical implementation can be limited by the need for stable resonator-coupler alignment. Here, we demonstrate a Rhodamine B-doped polymer WGM microring laser directly fabricated on an optical-fiber tip, eliminating the external resonator-fiber coupling interface at the sensing head. Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined for fabrication, while finite-difference time-domain simulations guide the microring laser design. The microlasers operate in air and water with thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively. Refractometric measurements in aqueous glucose solutions yield a bulk refractive index sensitivity of 364.95 nm/RIU and a detection limit of 2.47 x 10^(-4) RIU. Water-induced polymer changes and photobleaching are also investigated. This fiber-tip architecture provides a basis for probe-based refractometric sensing in environmental and biochemical applications.

papers.abs: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. papers.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
papers.abs: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 $\mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, this low-loss HfO$_{2}$ metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.

papers.abs: Ferroelectric phase transitions are driven by ion displacement-induced symmetry breaking, yet their chemical signatures are rarely probed directly at the atomic level. Here, we establish temperature-dependent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) as a powerful and quantitative probe of ferroelectric phase transitions by tracking ion migration-induced changes in local chemical environments. While ACPS exhibits only smooth trivial thermal broadening and shifts in core-level spectra, CCPS shows pronounced and enormously large temperature-dependent XPS anomalies across the ferroelectric transition, demonstrating that XPS is intrinsically sensitive to ferroelectric order. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. papers.abs: Long-range hoppings offer a powerful mechanism to engineer exotic topological phases beyond conventional tight-binding models. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a twofold topological phase transition driven by third-nearest-neighbor couplings in a one-dimensional phononic chain that emulates cis-polyacetylene. Tunable hopping parameters in highly structured aluminum plates allow us to observe the emergence of Dirac points, a valley pseudospin structure, and topological edge states. The experimental results are supported by non-equilibrium Green's function transport calculations. Our findings confirm the predicted long-range phase diagram and establish phononic metamaterials as a versatile platform for exploring topological phenomena beyond the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger paradigm.

papers.abs: Entanglement is conventionally defined through a Hilbert space bipartition on a fixed time slice. papers.abs: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry. papers.abs: In this work, we experimentally investigate the astigmatism induced by a birefringent crystal inside an optical cavity and demonstrate a geometric compensation strategy for structured modes carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM). We show that the astigmatism observed in the semimonolithic configuration can be fully compensated by introducing a third mirror to fold the cavity, thereby exploiting the geometric astigmatism arising from oblique incidence on the curved mirror. By performing a study of the resonator geometry, both theoretical and experimental results confirm that this approach enables the preservation of OAM between the pump beam and the converted signal and idler modes, providing an effective design strategy for birefringent optical cavities.

papers.abs: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth. papers.abs: Fiber-optic parametric amplifiers in a phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) configuration are well known for their low noise properties. Quantum mechanics dictates that these amplifiers can have a 0 dB noise figure (NF) (ratio of signal-to-noise ratio at the input and output of the amplifier) under certain conditions. However, for a dual-pump configuration, when the system is highly nonlinear, fully quantum calculations of NF become non-trivial. In such cases, semi-quantum models of NF evaluation exists, however, they are often complicated and resource intensive. To simplify that, in this work, first we use a semi-quantum NF calculation framework for the generation of numerically simulated input-output dataset of NF over a large parameter spaces. Then we use the data to train an optimized deep neural network (DNN) for rapid NF prediction. papers.title: Quantum enhanced beam displacement estimation: sensitivity limits, optimal probes, and measurement schemes
papers.abs: We investigate the ultimate sensitivity limits for measuring small transverse beam displacements and identify optimal strategies that attain them, using the framework of mode parameter estimation. We contrast two families of states with different resource constraints, using Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss mode pairs. First, for fixed total photon number states, the optimal state is identified and we show that it asymptotically approaches a rotated NOON state. The sensitivity bound is compared to that of an asymptotically optimal pure Gaussian state with fixed average photon number. Finally, we propose concrete measurement schemes using the method of moments and show that the twin-Fock state may provide a viable alternative to the rotated NOON state for this task. Our work provides a broader benchmark for developing practical strategies for spatial sensing at the quantum limit.

papers.abs: A metasurface is an electrically thin interface that controls the phase, amplitude and polarization of a wave, upon reflection or transmission. papers.abs: Inverse design of dielectric metasurfaces is powerful but labour-intensive: each new target requires choosing a parameterization and a figure of merit, managing compute resources, and critically assessing results that may be numerically unconverged, sensitive to fabrication errors or trapped in local optima. papers.abs: Exceptional bound states in the continuum (EBICs) arise when bound states in the continuum (BICs) with distinct intrinsic losses coalesce at exceptional points (EPs), combining continuum-embedded wave confinement with a non-analytic spectral response. papers.title: Nonuniform Time-bins for Making Raw QRNG Outputs Uniform
papers.abs: Random numbers play a vital role in scientific simulations and cryptography. Both randomness and security are critical requirements for random number generators (RNGs). However, classical RNGs often rely on mathematical assumptions that can compromise security, while quantum RNGs (QRNGs) face challenges, including non-uniform output due to the lack of specialized single-photon sources. In this work, we propose a QRNG model that generates uniformly distributed random numbers using a standard coherent photon source, without requiring heavy attenuation or post-processing. Although the raw data is theoretically free of bias, post-processing, if any, may be required to suppress any classical noise and device imperfections. The proposed method analytically equalizes the output probabilities under the assumed photon-arrival-time model, potentially reducing the need for heavy attenuation and post-processing to correct binning bias. papers.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
papers.abs: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starting, chip-scale ultrafast lasers.

papers.abs: Spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) has made significant progress in incoherent optical imaging and has been implemented through various experimental approaches. papers.title: Phase-Matched Design of Pinching-Antenna Elements on a 60-GHz Dielectric Rod Waveguide
papers.abs: The radiation of pinching antennas, dielectric elements placed on a dielectric waveguide, depends on the element shape. We explain it with a phase-matching, or prism-coupler, picture: the guided rod mode couples into the denser antenna plate at an angle set by the plate-mode effective index, about 31 degrees at 60 GHz, and radiates through the face it reaches first. This yields a simple sizing rule linking element height to contact length. Rectangular, isosceles and right-triangular elements of equal contact length and height are compared from 53 to 67 GHz in full-wave openEMS simulations including the waveguide-to-rod transitions. The rectangle peaks sharply at the rule, reaching 15.9 dBi. The right triangle keeps its gain within 0.7 dB and its side lobes at least 10 dB down over a two-to-one height range. At the rule, both outperform the isosceles element by 1.2 to 2.1 dB, and all remain matched.

papers.title: A Passive Intelligent Metasurface: A Network Model
papers.abs: Intelligent metasurfaces enable advanced wave manipulation, including negative refraction, focusing, beam splitting and beam steering, with significant potential for practical applications. However, conventional approaches often rely on active metamaterials with gain, or demand computationally intensive solutions of inverse problems to find the optimal configuration. In this work, we use the scattering framework of quantum graph theory to derive an exact, analytic expression for configuration of a passive metasurface that produces a prescribed reflected wave field. The metasurface terminates a periodic lattice of waveguides and consists of an array of channels, each a tube of length $\ell_m$ ending in a vertex whose scattering parameter $λ_m$ sets how much of the wave is lost to the wall. For any prescribed incident and reflected field, the exact lengths and scattering parameters follow channel by channel, in closed form, from the ratio of the wave amplitudes returning to and leaving the lattice, and the metasurface is passive whenever this ratio does not exceed unity in modulus.
