papers.title: Topological Acoustic Metamaterials with Synthetic Magnetism: Observation of Hofstadter Spectrum and Topological Edge States
papers.abs: Architected materials are increasingly used to implement topological dynamics, yet realizing the gauge fields and symmetries that protect the topology with purely passive elements remains the central practical challenge. Here we turn a previously proposed theoretical strategy into an integrated platform that accepts a theoretical model as input and returns a passive acoustic metamaterial with identical dynamics. We demonstrate it experimentally on the Hofstadter model at $θ= 2π/3$, fabricating a spin-Chern insulator whose two sectors carry Chern numbers $C_s = \pm 1$, and observe the predicted helical edge states.

papers.title: Ferroelectric Switching in x-cut MgO-doped Thin-Film Lithium Niobate: Implications for Periodic Poling and Domain-Wall Electronics
papers.abs: Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) revives a mature ferroelectric as a wafer-scale platform for integrated photonics and, increasingly, for domain-wall electronics such as nonvolatile memories and memristors. Both applications rely on controlled ferroelectric switching, which is poorly understood in TFLN: periodic poling consistently requires electric fields above 30~kV/mm, far above the coercive fields of about 21~kV/mm and 4.5~kV/mm of bulk congruent and 5~mol\% MgO-doped lithium niobate, respectively. Here, we present systematic ferroelectric hysteresis measurements on x-cut, 5~mol\% MgO-doped TFLN with coplanar electrodes as used for periodic poling, combining the positive-up-negative-down (PUND) method with second-harmonic microscopy (SHM). We obtain a spontaneous polarization of $(0.72\pm0.02)$~C/m$^2$, consistent with bulk values, while the coercive field varies between 24 and 40~kV/mm with the voltage ramp rate and depends on the electrode geometry. papers.title: From Fabrication Disorder to Quantum-Protocol Yield in Inverse-Designed Silicon Photonic Beam Splitters
papers.abs: Telecom-band silicon spin-photon qubits offer a promising platform for scalable quantum networks and distributed information processing, but their fixed emission wavelengths require compact, low-loss beam splitters with precise splitting and fabrication robustness. Conventional designs can face trade-offs between footprint, optical performance, and wavelength-specific operation. Here, we employ adjoint-based inverse design to optimize photonic geometries beyond conventional layouts, developing 1*2 Y-splitters and 2*2 directional couplers for the silicon T (1326 nm) and Al1 (1482.44 nm) spin-photon qubits. The devices achieve footprints of 2.9 and 26 um^2, respectively, with excess losses of 0.14-0.44 dB and back-reflection below 5*10^-4. We assess fabrication tolerance using 100-realization Monte Carlo simulations incorporating etch bias, line-edge roughness, thickness, and refractive-index variations. papers.title: Optical spectral asymmetry enables differential refractive-index sensing under near-perfect common-mode suppression in a single-cavity dual-comb fiber laser
papers.abs: Single-cavity dual-comb fiber lasers offer near-perfect common-mode suppression, but such suppression is generally expected to eliminate differential sensing signals. Here we show that optical spectral asymmetry enables differential refractive-index (RI) sensing despite near-perfect common-mode suppression. By integrating an intracavity multimode interference (MMI) fiber sensor into a shared cavity, two counter-propagating combs are simultaneously generated and interrogated, enabling differential RI sensing based on the repetition-frequency difference (Δfrep). This architecture achieves near-perfect common-mode suppression, reducing temperature-induced drift by more than two orders of magnitude compared with a conventional dual-cavity dual-comb system. Spectral analysis reveals that optical spectral asymmetry gives rise to asymmetric repetition-frequency responses through cavity dispersion, thereby providing the physical origin of the differential sensing signal. papers.title: Scan-less Hyperspectral Polarimetric Imaging Using Dual-Comb Single-Pixel Imaging
papers.abs: Spectroscopic polarimetry enables detailed characterization of light-matter interactions by combining spectral and polarization information, yet conventional implementations rely on mechanical polarization modulation and are difficult to extend to fast, broadband imaging. Dual-comb spectroscopic polarimetry (DCSP) addresses these limitations by providing rapid, modulation-free access to polarization-resolved amplitude and phase spectra, but has so far been limited to point-based measurements. In this work, we introduce dual-comb spectro-polarimetric single-pixel imaging (DCSP-SPI), a new framework that combines DCSP with structured illumination and single-pixel detection to achieve scan-less hyperspectral polarimetric imaging without a camera. By exploiting the intrinsic amplitude and phase sensitivity of dual-comb interferometry, spectrally resolved images of the amplitude ratio psi and phase difference delta are reconstructed across a broad optical spectrum. papers.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
papers.abs: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. With our approach, we show that populating quantum dots does not require engineered reservoirs, source/drain bias, ohmic contacts, or in-situ doping. As a result, the number of gates can be kept minimal and the fabrication process can be simplified. papers.title: Controlling the Sign and Magnitude of the Thermoreflectance Coefficient of Gold-MoS$_2$ Metamaterials
papers.abs: Heating a material changes how much light it reflects. This effect, quantified by the thermoreflectance coefficient $C_\mathrm{TR}$, enables temperature sensing, while it is a nuisance for situations where constant reflection is crucial. Whereas temperature detection requires a large $C_\mathrm{TR}$, the latter situation demands it to be as close to zero as possible. Controlling the $C_\mathrm{TR}$ has so far relied on the selection of materials and wavelengths, rather than engineering the coefficient itself. This work demonstrates that the $C_\mathrm{TR}$ of a 50 nm thin gold film on SiO$_2$/Si can be controlled in sign and magnitude by an ultrathin ($<$8 nm) MoS$_2$ film underneath it. Time-resolved thermoreflectance measurements reveal suppression, sign inversion, and revival of the thermoreflectance signal, controlled by three knobs: ($i$) the buried MoS$_2$ thickness, ($ii$) probe wavelength, and ($iii$) ambient temperature. papers.title: Experimental demonstration of phase-conjugated twin-wave coherent reception over 100 km with injection locking assisted phase stabilization
papers.abs: Recovering complex optical signals with high sensitivity is central to coherent communication and sensing. Beyond conventional homodyne and heterodyne reception, phase-conjugate twin-wave encoding and phase-sensitive joint detection offer an alternative strategy with enhanced sensitivity. Extending this approach to long-distance transmission of high-order-modulated signals is challenging because optical phase coherence must be maintained at the receiver. Here we experimentally demonstrate injection-locking-assisted phase-conjugated twin-wave reception of 200-MBaud signals with modulation formats up to 256-QAM over 100 km of optical fiber. Optical injection locking regenerates the local oscillator (LO) from a reference transmitted through the 16 dB-loss link, while pilot-assisted optical feedback stabilizes the relative signal-LO phase, enabling coherent combining of the phase-conjugated twin waves at a single balanced photodetector. papers.title: Propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam with conserved topology
papers.abs: We report the generation and control of a propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam through the digitally controlled superposition of a first-order petal- and Gaussian- mode each marked with orthogonal polarizations. We present a detailed analysis of the spatial and polarization profiles and unveil their intricate topological features, showing that they have properties that are invariant to the propagation dynamics, in addition to their preserved intensity. The differential Gouy phase between the spatial components is shown to rotate the great circle traced by the polarisation distribution on the Poincaré sphere. Finally, we assess the beams for laser cutting and optical trapping, highlighting the relevance of topological structured light to these applications.

papers.title: Spin-induced lateral acoustic forces on chiral and achiral particles
papers.abs: Acoustic spin enables intriguing chiral sound-matter interactions, yet its mechanical consequences remain much less explored. Here, we demonstrate spin-induced lateral acoustic forces on chiral and achiral particles coupled to a substrate. Under plane-wave incidence, left- and right-handed chiral particles scatter fields with opposite acoustic spin that selectively couple to counterpropagating guided waves, generating lateral forces of opposite signs on the enantiomers. The lateral forces can also be realized for achiral particles by employing acoustic vortex-beam illumination. We experimentally validate the spin-dependent excitation of guided waves and lateral forces. Our results provide a route to spin-controlled acoustic manipulation and chirality-selective particle transport.

papers.title: Learning to read residual images for single-pixel photography
papers.abs: Continuous video scales in cost with camera count, resolution and recording duration, yet many monitoring tasks seek events rather than complete images and can operate on a compact single-pixel measurement stream. Recovering a chosen interval as video is then desirable, but at 0.24\% of the pixel count the scene correlation image looks like noise and per-clip optimization takes minutes. Correlating the residual of an estimate with the coding patterns nevertheless gives a residual image, the gradient of a centered measurement loss. Lifted through a pretrained video decoder, its agreement with the true error exceeds that of control decoders. Video-latent inversion (VLI) then outperforms frame-wise image-latent reconstruction at 1{,}000 bucket values. papers.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
papers.abs: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. Energetic electrons deposit energy in silicon, producing nonequilibrium carriers that perturb the semiconductor surface potential and electric displacement across the adjacent aqueous interface. papers.title: Learned optical compression for single-pixel quantitative phase imaging
papers.abs: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) reveals optical path-length variations in transparent objects but typically relies on spatially resolved intensity measurements. Here we numerically and experimentally demonstrate learned optical compression for single-pixel QPI, jointly optimizing a diffractive encoder and a digital neural decoder to concentrate reconstruction-relevant phase information into a compact measurement vector. A single reconfigurable phase-modulation plane sequentially displays the learned encoding patterns, which are independent of the input object, each yielding one scalar intensity measurement. Operating at a visible wavelength, the experimental system reconstructs quantitative phase images of unknown objects with ~40-fold dimensional compression, using only 2.55% as many intensity measurements as reconstructed pixels. Experimental blind testing on handwritten digits and grating-like phase objects achieves mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.945 and 0.848, respectively. papers.title: Structural and Optical Properties of PVP-Modified ZnS Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
papers.abs: Pristine and PVP-modified ZnS nanoparticles were investigated to examine how PVP addition affects structural, surface, optical, and methylene blue (MB) decolorization properties. X-ray diffraction confirmed cubic zinc-blende ZnS in all samples, with apparent Scherrer coherent-domain sizes of 3.10-3.31 nm. Electron microscopy revealed agglomeration, while HRTEM and electron diffraction confirmed locally crystalline regions in S1 and S4. The estimated direct Tauc gap decreased from 3.69 eV for S1 to 3.58 eV for S4. Between 100 and 300 K, the principal TO-like Raman band softened on heating, while visible photoluminescence changed predominantly within the overlapping green-yellow region. After 210 min under 254 nm irradiation, MB-band losses near 664 nm reached 19.33%, 58.18%, 70.00%, and 94.42% for S1-S4, compared with 6.58% for the catalyst-free control. PVP modification therefore alters optical and dye-decolorization responses while preserving the principal ZnS phase; however, dye-band attenuation alone does not establish complete mineralization.

papers.title: PETE: A Hybrid Photonic and Electronic Thermoelectric Device for Direct Heat-to-Electricity Conversion
papers.abs: Photonic heat engines can achieve high conversion efficiencies, but their far-field power density is constrained by the blackbody limit. Near-field devices overcome this limitation through photon tunneling across a nanoscale vacuum gap; however, the mechanical spacers required to maintain this gap introduce parasitic heat conduction. We propose PETE (Photonic and Electronic Thermoelectric), a hybrid solid-state architecture in which thermoelectric generator (TEG) legs replace passive spacers. The legs simultaneously maintain the near-field gap and convert conducted heat into electricity. We evaluate PETE using an indium tin oxide emitter, an indium arsenide photovoltaic cell, and TaFeSb- and ZrNiSn-based Half-Heusler thermoelectric materials. At a hot-side temperature of 977K, the device achieves a power density of 18.6 W$\cdot$cm$^{-2}$ at 19.76% efficiency. This power density is approximately twice that of either the standalone near-field thermophotovoltaic device or the standalone TEG, while the efficiency is 44% higher than that of the standalone TEG. papers.abs: Computational imaging can reduce the acquisition burden when the system is designed around task-relevant information rather than complete image recovery. We investigate this framework for sparse-view planar X-ray tomography (XCT) of layered objects, using measurement of the axial termination gap (ATG) of back-drilled printed-circuit-board (PCB) vias as a representative task. Instead of using 3D reconstruction, the proposed method estimates ATG directly from polychromatic projection data through a physics-based sensitivity model. A gated hierarchical estimator first fits ATG together with radiometric perturbations and selectively introduces global geometry and specimen-warp models only when a reduced chi-squared adequacy test and Bayesian information criterion justify the added degrees of freedom. The same low-dimensional perturbation model is incorporated into marginalized Fisher-information analyses, yielding task-specific conditional and calibration-aware Cram'er-Rao bounds. papers.title: Superradiance fingerprints of moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel
papers.abs: Hybrid moiré excitons form a dense array of electrically tunable single-photon emitters, entailing cooperative optical responses with intriguing consequences. With the strong dipole-dipole interaction, they also realize Bose-Hubbard quantum simulators of emergent correlated matter such as Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC). Here we reveal the characteristic cooperative radiation from condensates of hybrid moiré excitons in twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayers. In each individual moiré trap, the layer hybridization selection rule dictates that the ground-state exciton is a quantum emitter of orbital-angular-momentum photons, with an exceptionally long radiative lifetime. Ground-state emission becomes pronounced only upon forming condensates, where inter-sublattice dipole attraction and intra-sublattice repulsion together lead to the coexistence of exciton and biexciton BEC with comparable weights. The biexciton (molecular-type) BEC decays through superradiance of path-entangled biphotons, whereas the exciton (atomic-type) BEC is dark at rest and becomes superradiant when it carries a supercurrent.

papers.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
papers.abs: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.

Within the random-phase approximation, we analyse the density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes and their Landau damping, and Friedel oscillations, considering both small and arbitrary momentum transfers. In our companion work, arXiv:2610.18629, we investigated pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals, with and without a quadratic correction to their dispersion, as well as Hopf and Weyl semimetals. Comparing these systems allows us to elucidate the distinct roles of band dispersions and eigenstates in shaping collective charge dynamics. papers.title: Cooling-path-selected self-assembly of telecom InAsP quantum dots
papers.abs: Epitaxial quantum dots are leading solid-state sources of quantum light, but reproducible growth on indium phosphide (InP) remains challenging because dot-formation windows are narrow and emission wavelengths are difficult to predict. Here we report a new epitaxial route for InAsP quantum dots on InP(001), in which the cooling path selects the final morphology without intentional deposition of group-III dot material. High-temperature As exposure forms a shallow near-surface InAsP layer through As-P exchange; the cooling path and continued As supply determine whether three-dimensional islands form. Surface-sensitive spectroscopy shows near-surface As enrichment, while cross-sectional STEM/EELS identifies graded, As-rich InAsP islands. The capped emitters span 1.2-1.6 micrometers, with single-photon emission observed up to 100 K. Across 20 wafers, the surface-effective exchange dose D provides a practical calibration for targeting the median emission wavelength. These results establish cooling as an active epitaxial step for telecom InAsP quantum-dot formation and wavelength control.

papers.title: Relaxation characteristics and spectral compression in the system of coupled radiating oscillators
papers.abs: The electromagnetic response of two identical coupled oscillators to an ultrashort pulse is investigated. Due to interference between the radiation emitted by the constituent oscillators, the temporal dynamics of the dipole radiation from the system are governed by a nontrivial relationship between their dipole moment amplitudes and differ markedly from those of an isolated oscillator. An analysis based on coupled-mode theory demonstrates that, under appropriate conditions, the energy of an incident ultrashort pulse can be converted into quasi-monochromatic radiation with high efficiency. The theoretical results are supported by qualitative numerical simulations of thin conductive rods resonant in the terahertz frequency range and separated by a deeply subwavelength distance, providing a physical realization of the coupled radiating-oscillator system.

papers.abs: We show that encoding superconducting qubits as dual-rail or spin-locked transmons lets a metamaterial waveguide couple them all-to-all while suppressing the spurious entanglement that burdens shared-mode architectures, a step toward the non-local connectivity that quantum low-density parity-check codes require. In a bare-transmon architecture, the dispersive coupling between each populated mode and every idle qubit attached to it entangles spectators with the gate, and cancelling it by dynamical decoupling lengthens every gate. The encoding suppresses this coupling at the hardware level, from second to fourth order in the inverse qubit--mode detuning. papers.abs: Highly nonlinear phenomena, where macroscopic changes are triggered by microscopic perturbations, are ubiquitous in complex systems ranging from epidemic spreading to neural networks. However, this nonlinearity is typically determined by material composition, making this behavior challenging to tune for adaptive sensing, imaging, and neuromorphic applications. Here, we demonstrate giant optical magnetic field gated threshold and nonlinearity in lanthanide doped nanoparticles. We exploit the distinct quantum selection rules of the avalanche process: while the energy looping cycles of excited state absorption and cross relaxation are primarily electrically driven, the seed excitation, ground state absorption, is a mixed transition permitting magnetic dipole interaction. papers.title: Nonlinear Dynamics in Periodically Distributed Fibre Amplification Systems
papers.abs: We investigate effects of longitudinally varying nonlinearity on periodically distributed amplification systems in optical fibres. Emphasis is made on configurations in which the nonlinear coefficient exponentially grows or decays along the propagation distance, while the group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) coefficient is held constant. Such systems are of practical relevance to the design of highly efficient nonlinear devices, including broadband light sources and advanced amplification schemes, where precise management of the interplay between the GVD, nonlinearity, and gain is essential. Adopting the known generic integrability condition, we derive exact analytical expressions for the evolution of the optical field in the presence of the tailored nonlinearity profiles and periodically distributed gain. papers.title: Optimal Fan-Out and Break-Even Routing Loss in Waveguide-Integrated Ge-on-Si SPAD Arrays
papers.abs: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts. We quantify this trade-off with the asymptotic count-based information rate, which prices dark counts and dead time in one unit and is attained by an optimally weighted moment estimator. For a non-paralyzable pixel, the information per pre-dead-time signal event peaks at a signal rate $y^*=\sqrt{D(D+1/τ)}$ with exact efficiency $(\sqrt{1+Dτ}-\sqrt{Dτ})^2$, which sets the optimal fan-out and a critical flux above which equal splitting is optimal. We then compare four routing architectures on 64 simulated 16-pixel arrays: an equal passive tree, static trees (uncalibrated, and an idealized calibration-informed benchmark), an ideal programmable tree, and a thermo-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) tree with 1.32 dB excess loss. papers.abs: Scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) is a versatile tool for probing optical properties at deeply subwavelength scales. Here, we generalize this framework to multilayer samples using two equivalent methods: a generalized image charge method and a Fourier integral method. papers.abs: Piezoelectric resonators have emerged as promising energy-storage elements for compact high-frequency DC-DC power converters. Finite-element simulations show that a square plate excites numerous lateral spurious modes near the principal shear resonance. In contrast, a curved asymmetric plate outline redistributes the lateral acoustic boundary conditions and reduces electrically visible spurious responses. papers.title: Experimental Realization of a Nonreciprocal Quantum Battery
papers.abs: Quantum batteries promise faster and more efficient energy storage and extraction by harnessing quantum mechanics, serving as essential building blocks for future quantum devices. A key practical requirement-unidirectional energy flow during charging-is straightforward in classical batteries via potential difference, yet remains a major challenge in the quantum regime due to the inherent reciprocity of coherent coupling. Here, we realize the first backflow-free, nonreciprocal quantum battery in the few-quantum regime, implemented in a highly controlled trapped-ion system via a qubit-reservoir engineering technique. By subtly tailoring quantum interference between coherent and dissipative couplings of two laser-cooled motional modes, we achieve strictly unidirectional energy flow from the charger to the battery. We observe maximum charging power at an exceptional point and demonstrate a complete charge-discharge cycle with unitary work extraction. papers.title: Energy-Centroid Trembling near Exceptional Points in Photonic Time Crystals
papers.abs: In a photonic time crystal with a modulated Lorentz restoring coefficient, modulation reweights the potential energy of the polarization and loss drains its kinetic energy; when these sectors are offset within a pulse, the energy centroid trembles in every cycle while the Poynting-flux velocity stays bounded. Near the gap-edge exceptional point the mode geometry amplifies these offsets, and for a narrow-band pulse on one passband Floquet branch the trembling-velocity amplitude generically grows as the inverse square root of the momentum detuning, rounded by finite bandwidth. Loss modulated in phase or in antiphase with the restoring coefficient can change the trembling coefficient while the band-slope and Petermann coefficients barely move. In the lossy example studied, a forward field pulse launched with the polarization at rest exhibits delayed bursts near the beat recurrence after substantial energy loss, with monochromatic amplitudes following the inverse three-halves power of the detuning over the computed range. papers.title: Photon-loss tolerance of the surface-GKP code with anti-photon-loss decoding
papers.abs: Photon loss somewhat limits fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing. We investigate its effect on finite-energy Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) states by modeling the pure-loss channel directly. We obtain photon-loss threshold estimates for the surface-GKP code using nearest-lattice-point inner GKP decoding and minimum-weight perfect matching for the outer surface code. For GKP states with $ε=0.01$ and $ε=0.05$, corresponding to GKP squeezing of $20$ and $13\,\mathrm{dB}$, the estimated thresholds are $γ^\ast=5.5\%$ ($0.24\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $γ^\ast=5.9\%$ ($0.26\,\mathrm{dB}$), respectively. We then introduce an anti-photon-loss inner decoder that compensates for the contraction of the measured quadrature. It increases the corresponding threshold estimates to $γ^\ast=9.8\%$ ($0.45\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $γ^\ast=6.3\%$ ($0.28\,\mathrm{dB}$). Our results highlight the importance of accounting for loss-induced lattice contraction in inner decoding and demonstrate that quadrature compensation enhances the photon-loss tolerance of surface-GKP codes for both high- and moderate-quality GKP

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Theory of Surface Emitting Jackiw-Rebbi States
papers.abs: Topological interface states in open photonic systems combine spatial localization at domain walls with temporal confinement characterized by a radiative quality factor. Here, we develop a non-Hermitian Dirac formalism for surface-emitting Jackiw-Rebbi states in dielectric metagratings. We show how varying the local amplitude of the lattice perturbation shapes the complex Dirac mass profile, enabling control over the quality factors and far-field radiation patterns of the interface states, while preserving their topological character. Applying this framework to a metagrating with second-order Brillouin-zone folding, we design a spatially graded superlattice perturbation that supports interface states with quality factors exceeding 10$^4$ and Hermite-Gaussian beam emission. These results establish superlattice perturbations as a strategy for topological beam shaping and offer a route toward high-Q topological surface emitters.

papers.title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI
papers.abs: A central obstacle in realizing color center cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is inhomogeneity, or disorder, among individual emitters. As the number of emitters increases, so does the complexity of the experimental data, making it difficult to quantify the present physical mechanisms of disorder. Here we introduce an artificial intelligence-driven model discovery framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent, equipped with tools and a structured workflow, proposes candidate Hamiltonian and Lindbladian models, generates computational tools, and quantitatively evaluates competing physical hypotheses. We apply the workflow to three previously published experimental cavity-QED datasets collected from color centers in diamond and silicon carbide. Across the experiments, the agent successfully identifies physical models for the system and characterizes the disorder. In assessing reproducibility, we find that run-to-run variability is concentrated primarily in the research plan generation step, while the computational analysis itself is substantially more consistent. papers.title: Enhanced shortcuts to adiabaticity in an interacting giant-atom-atomic-waveguide system
papers.abs: In realistic quantum systems, isolated few-level models usually provide only an approximate description, since the controlled subsystem is generally coupled to additional degrees of freedom. As a result, a quantum control scheme designed for an isolated system may lose its original performance in a more complex coupled setting. Here, we consider a giant atom coupled to an interacting atomic waveguide and investigate enhanced shortcuts to adiabaticity (eSTA) in such a structured system. As a first step, a weak-coupling perturbative analysis identifies how changes in the initial and target states, together with dynamical transitions, contribute to the fidelity loss. Starting from a shortcut to adiabaticity control scheme for the uncoupled system, the enhanced STA correction improves the final fidelity by modifying only the giant-atom control fields. This improvement is found for both periodic and open boundary conditions of the atomic waveguide. The results demonstrate a way to design an eSTA protocol for an interacting composite system.

papers.abs: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is used to elucidate the band structure of (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x, a new magnetic quantum material grown using molecular beam epitaxy that has a Curie temperature (TC) above 100K, much higher than those reported for other materials of the MnxSb2-xTe4 class. Conflicting and sparse theory and experiments, as well as the complex disordered structure of the materials make it difficult to establish their topological nature. Here we explore this question by performing ARPES studies for two samples with x=0.65 and x=0.92, respectively. Images of the band structures of these two samples were acquired using photon energy dependent studies. The bulk and surface states of this complex material system, and the effects of composition on the band structure were investigated. papers.abs: We experimentally demonstrate a 100-m long fiber Sagnac gyroscope employing imaginary weak-value amplification (IWVA) to enhance the optical readout response to rotation. A Sagnac-induced polarization phase is converted into a measurable spectral response through polarization post-selection and spectrally resolved detection. By varying the post-selection angle, we characterize the gyroscope response over the experimentally accessible rotation-rate range. The response increases systematically toward orthogonal post-selection, yielding a maximum experimental enhancement of approximately 13 times relative to a fixed reference configuration without postselection. papers.title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?
papers.abs: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. When the data needed for an answer are missing, the model should say so. We test representation invariance and abstention on measured optical spectra of silicon metasurfaces (MOCLIP) and gold nanoparticles, with labels computed from the data. Each spectrum is shown as four tables (nm, $μ$m, scientific notation, eV) and two plots (nm, eV), and partial spectra remove data inside or outside the queried range. We evaluate the decision models d3-nano and Jev 1.13, three GPT-6 Luna configurations and the Qwen3.5-2B base model. Changing only the representation moves accuracy by up to 41 percentage points within one model, mostly on photon-energy tables and plots. With the same evidence, asking in photon energy instead of wavelength helps some model-view pairs by 16-50 points and hurts others by up to 25. papers.title: Nonperturbative theory of thin-vapor-layer linear optical properties: towards the optimal design of alkali-metal vapor nanocells
papers.abs: Hot alkali-metal vapors confined inside nanometer-thick spectroscopic cells are highly suitable media for miniature and cheap frequency standards, magnetometers and atomic sensors. Yet their linear optical properties at low to moderate atomic densities are not fully understood. The main reason is the complex, strongly nonlocal optical response of such systems to resonant radiation, which arises from the free motion of atoms and their collisions with the walls. To date, calculations of reflection and transmission spectra of these cells have been restricted to perturbation theory in the atomic density for the case of quenching atom-wall collisions, which has substantially limited their practical use. Here we introduce a rigorous numerical approach for computing thin-vapor-layer spectra that accurately accounts for the nonlocal optical response at arbitrary optical density and layer thickness. papers.title: BEEF: A Hybrid Integrated Photonic Simulation Framework
papers.abs: A Python framework is presented that retains first-principles electromagnetic modeling while extending simulation to devices whose length and geometric complexity place them beyond the practical reach of either method alone. The Bridged Engine for eigenmode expansion (EME) and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) (BEEF) partitions a device into sections which are simulated using either EME or FDTD independently developed Maxwell solvers depending on what best suits each section's geometry, and cascades the resulting responses. BEEF calibrates the EME propagation constants against FDTD-measured phase accumulation, providing a mode identity verification diagnostic across solver interfaces. For a 2x2 multimode-interference splitter, the hybrid result agrees with full-device FDTD to within 0.59% (bar) and 0.76% (cross) across the C-band; a tapered variant agrees to within 0.87% and 2.01%, respectively. papers.title: Quantum dynamics of ultrasmall magnetic skyrmions in atomic-defect landscapes
papers.abs: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~Å. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~$μ$eV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. papers.title: Coherent transduction and dynamical back-action between light and millimeter waves
papers.abs: Electro-optic transduction can bypass the loss and noise of electronic frequency conversion at millimeter-wave frequencies by parametrically converting signals onto low-loss, low-noise optical carriers, with coupling rates that grow with frequency. Exploiting this growth, however, requires shrinking both the millimeter-wave and optical resonators while preserving their quality factors and spatial overlap, which has not yet been achieved. Here, we demonstrate a triply resonant transducer whose optical and millimeter-wave resonators have comparable dimensions and minimal mode volumes. Coupled lithium niobate Fabry-Pérot cavities, with free spectral ranges above 650 GHz and quality factors up to $10^6$, form a photonic molecule integrated with a quarter-wave gold resonator at 263 GHz. The device reaches a vacuum electro-optic coupling rate $g_0/2π\approx 60$ kHz, six times larger than previous millimeter-wave transducers and sixty times larger than at microwave frequencies. papers.title: Animated Ultraviolet Holography via Programmable Nonlinear Phase Transfer
papers.abs: Dynamic and programmable control of ultraviolet (UV) light remains challenging because of conventional high material absorption and the limited functionality of optics such as lenses, mirrors or filters, and optoelectronic devices, such as spatial phase modulators, over the UV range. Here, by employing the concept of virtual metasurfaces based on arrays of programmable optical patterns on a 600-nm-thick lithium niobate film as the nonlinear medium, we demonstrate nonlinear phase transfer, generating programmable holography in the UV range. This arrangement provides a unique platform for generating animated holograms. A spatial light modulator encodes a computer-generated phase distribution onto a longer-wavelength pump beam, while second-harmonic generation transfers the programmed spatial phase to the UV field through the quadratic nonlinear interaction. Importantly, the nonlinear film serves as a simple frequency-conversion interface, eliminating the need for nanostructure patterning or direct UV spatial modulation. papers.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
papers.abs: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. By measuring the transmitted probe electric field as a function of pump-probe delay, we directly retrieve the pump-induced phase shift and its temporal evolution while retaining sensitivity to changes in absorption. papers.title: Benchmarking Single-Photon Sources for Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abs: Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD) enables secure communication without trusting the measurement devices, but its performance critically depends on the quality of the employed photon sources. We compare MDI-QKD implementations based on Weak Coherent Pulses (WCPs) with those employing Quantum Dot (QD) single-photon sources. WCP-based schemes are fundamentally limited by Poissonian photon-number statistics, imposing a trade-off between single- and multi-photon emissions, whereas QD sources exhibit sub-Poissonian statistics with low antibunching parameter $g^{(2)}(0)$. Using a decoy-state analysis for both source types, we find that even at moderate mean photon numbers, QD-based implementations outperform the best-case WCP configuration - where the mean photon number is optimised at each transmission distance - across the full range of transmission distances. papers.title: Focusing through coupled multimode fibers for miniaturized single-atom tweezer arrays
papers.abs: Real-world deployment of quantum technologies requires systems in low SWaP-C packages. Quantum platforms based on ultracold atoms typically trap and control atoms with optical tweezers using light focused through bulky objective lenses, which are costly and sensitive to misalignment. Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer a compact route to focusing light, but their use in forming optical tweezers for cold atoms has been limited to a single fiber. Here we use a 2x1 MMF fused coupler to obtain two independent control paths sharing a common distal facet. We form near-diffraction-limited tweezers through each channel, suppress interference by applying a small frequency offset between the channels, and demonstrate that the tweezer separation is insensitive to misalignment of the input coupling. This work provides a route to reconfigurable single-atom arrays in low SWaP-C environments.

papers.abs: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. papers.title: Magnetic control of reflectionless states and an intrinsic-mode exceptional point in a magnon-phonon coupling system
papers.abs: Reflectionless states (RLs) and exceptional points (EPs) are hallmark singular responses of non-Hermitian systems, with potential applications in sensing, wave control, and energy manipulation. Yet, realizing and independently tuning these states in a compact integrated platform remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate two-dimensional magnetic control of RLs and EPs in an on-chip magnon-phonon system based on a FeGaB-32 degree-YX-LiNbO3 heterostructure. The magnetic-field magnitude tunes the magnon-phonon detuning, driving a low-loss reflection zero across the real-frequency axis and producing two field-tunable RLs with near-vanishing reflection. A closed contour of the experimentally measured complex S11 around the reflection-zero singularity accumulates a -2pi phase winding. Independently, rotating the magnetic field tunes the magnon-phonon coupling strength, driving the intrinsic magnon-phonon eigenmode spectrum across an exceptional point, identified by the exchange between real-part and imaginary-part eigenvalue splitting. papers.title: Fabry-Pérot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
papers.abs: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.

papers.abs: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. papers.title: A Highly Nondegenerate Photon-Pair Source for Detector-Matched Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abs: In a commercial entanglement-distribution system over telecom fibre, the single-photon detectors are the largest part of the hardware cost. In entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD), both photons of each pair must be detected. With two telecom photons, each arm needs either an InGaAs single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) of low efficiency or a superconducting nanowire single-photon detector (SNSPD) with its own cryostat. We study a highly nondegenerate photon-pair source that needs a telecom detector on one arm only. Two periodically poled KTiOPO$_4$ (ppKTP) crystals pumped at 405~nm emit pairs at 548 and 1550~nm. A Si-SPAD with 82\% efficiency detects the 548~nm photon at the source node, and only the 1550~nm photon travels through fibre. A first, unoptimised module in a polarisation-correlated configuration generates about $1.5\times10^6$ pairs/s per mW of pump power. It collects 13\% of the pairs on the 548~nm arm and 23\% on the 1550~nm arm. papers.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
papers.abs: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

papers.title: Windowed Catodyne Measurements: Continuum Approximation versus Exact Discrete Photon-Number Treatment
papers.abs: We analyze a family of measurements obtained by retaining only a finite window of the photon-sum variable in catodyne detection, where a Schrödinger cat state serves as the local oscillator. In the continuum approximation, the window half-width appears to act as a continuous knob for coherence. However, a treatment on the discrete photon-number lattice shows that, in the strong-LO regime, the coherence conditioned on the difference outcome is not suppressed by the window. The exact parity-sensitive success probability is a staircase function of and , whose plateau structure and magnitude the continuum formulas fail to capture, especially for small and narrow windows. For remote preparation of cat states, an exact calculation with a finitely squeezed resource shows that the remote state keeps a purity close to one when x is resolved, and loses purity mainly when x is not recorded. Our results clarify where the continuum approximation of catodyne detection can be trusted and where the discrete photon-number structure must be used.

papers.abs: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes in optical response across the chalcogen series. papers.title: The Generalized Twin Image: Understanding Regularized Phase Retrieval
papers.abs: Image priors can dramatically improve phase retrieval reconstruction, but their effectiveness strongly varies between imaging modalities. We introduce the generalized twin image, which extends the classical twin-image ambiguity from Fourier phase retrieval to any invertible sensing operator, to understand this effectiveness. The ambiguity extends to undersampled and oversampled measurements, remaining exact under undersampling and for oversampled coded Fourier measurements. We show that it provides a simple criterion to assess regularization effectiveness: the image prior should favor the ground truth over its generalized twin image. We propose the total-variation ratio as a simple measure of this preference, and derive closed-form estimates for structured random phase retrieval models. Experiments with a pretrained denoiser demonstrate that the ratio predicts regularized reconstruction performance across different sensing models.

papers.title: Potentials of individual atoms by convergent beam electron diffraction
papers.abs: In convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) on two-dimensional (2D) materials, the intensity distributions within the individual CBED spots map the local atomic arrangements within the probed region. In this study we demonstrate that the average intensities within the CBED spots essentially depend on the scattering parameters by a single atom, thus, offering the possibility of the direct measurement of such parameters. Scattering potential of an individual atom can be approximated by the Gaussian function and its parameters, the standard deviation and the maximal phase shift, can be recovered from the ratio of the intensities in the zero- and higher orders spots in CBED pattern. In order to demonstrate this, we simulated CBED patterns and extracted the atomic scattering parameters from such patterns. In the simulated examples, no weak phase object approximation is applied and the proposed method provides accurate results even for materials with large phase shifts up to 1.5 rad, as for example tungsten. papers.abs: The reconfigurable generation of complex structured terahertz (THz) fields, and vector beams in particular, remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose a novel all-dielectric cascaded-metasurface scheme for the reconfigurable generation of THz spiral vector beams. By combining an isotropic phase-compensation layer with an anisotropic circular-polarization-sensitive layer, together with a new phase design tailored to spiral beams, we achieve independent control of the left- and right-handed circularly polarized (LCP and RCP) components through the relative rotation angle between the two layers. Under linearly polarized THz wave illumination, THz vector beams with switchable spiral numbers of 1-3 and reversible circular-polarization handedness are demonstrated at frequencies around 0.9 THz. Moreover, owing to the longitudinal evolution characteristic of spiral beams, the three generated THz vector beams exhibit azimuthal rotations of 279.9°, 125.7° and 75.5°, respectively, along the propagation direction. papers.title: Loss-aware optimization of realistic GKP gid states
papers.abs: Realistic preparation of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states, the prime candidates for quantum computation with bosonic systems, is inevitably burdened by photon loss. We show how taking this loss into account can lead to more robust quantum states, thereby diminishing its negative influence. Using GKP squeezing as an operational figure of merit, we formulate a loss-aware optimization procedure based on the ground state representation of GKP states. Numerical simulations for square, hexagonal, and asymmetric GKP states show that the optimal preparation generally requires a different initial grid spacing than that of the desired ideal code state. For symmetric and hexagonal lattices, the optimal parameters asymptotically follow the simple scaling relation. The optimized states exhibit better GKP squeezing and greater resilience to losses. These results provide a simple and experimentally relevant strategy for improving realistic photonic GKP state preparation in the presence of known photon loss.

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Spectral Topology Shaped by Memory
papers.abs: Non-Hermitian spectral topology has transformed our understanding of bulk--boundary correspondence in open systems, yet its exploration has largely remained within the Markovian regime of instantaneous coupling. Here, we reveal how memory shapes non-Hermitian spectral topology by extending coupling asymmetry from space to time. Spatiotemporal nonreciprocity and memory-induced spectral multivaluedness give rise to nontrivial spectral topology on multi-sheeted Riemann surfaces, governed by both spatial connectivity and interaction history. Coherent interference among long-range memory channels can induce anomalous spectral winding and skin localization opposite to the dominant-coupling direction. Moreover, asymmetric retardation alone can generate non-Hermitian spectral topology and skin accumulation even in the absence of spatial coupling asymmetry. Channel dissipation further drives topological transitions that reverse the skin effect, with a critical point at matched channel and lattice decay rates. papers.abs: Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states are key resources for fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing, but their conditional preparation via Gaussian boson sampling involves a trade-off between source count and photon-number resolution. Distributing heralding photons across more measured modes reduces the resolution required per mode, yet increases the number of simultaneously operated squeezed sources in fully squeezed spatial architectures. Using an end-to-end differentiable Bargmann framework, we find that TDM circuits reusing one or two squeezed sources achieve fidelities comparable to fully squeezed spatial circuits across several configurations. papers.title: Input-dependent Neuromodulation Enhances Mixed-Signal Neuromorphic Hardware
papers.abs: Gating mechanisms allow a fixed neural network to adapt its computation to the current input by dynamically modulating its effective parameters. In the brain, neuromodulation uses this principle to move neural circuits between dynamical regimes, and deep learning exploits input-dependent gating, e.g., in gated recurrent networks and self-attention. Input-dependent modulation has also recently been shown to improve spiking neural networks, with particularly strong benefits in small, parameter-limited ones. This makes neuromodulation especially promising for neuromorphic processors at the edge, where area, memory and energy budgets constrain network size, while circuit physics limits parameter precision. Here we demonstrate input-dependent, within-trial neuromodulation of a spiking recurrent neural network on a mixed-signal neuromorphic processor. papers.title: Non-contact temperature sensing and optical scatter in cryogenically-cooled crystalline silicon
papers.abs: Cryogenic crystalline silicon is a promising optical material for next generation gravitational-wave detectors due to its low mechanical loss (a driver of thermal noise), high thermal conductivity and zero coefficient of thermal expansion at 123 K. In this paper, we report on the design and results of an experiment to measure the temperature of a flat-flat uncoated crystalline silicon sample using a non-contact sensing method relying on interference (optical fringes) made from reflections between the front and back surfaces. We also propose a scheme for implementation of this technique for cryogenic test masses in future gravitational-wave detectors such as Einstein Telescope and LIGO Voyager. Additionally, we characterize the optical scattering of the sample in vacuum at cryogenic temperatures by using a high-sensitivity infrared camera. We measured relatively constant scatter with an average bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of $(4.43\pm0.2)\times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{sr^{-1}}$ at a scattering angle of $θ_{s} = 7.5^\circ$ over the (cold-plate) temperature range of

papers.title: Intensity-Domain Demultiplexing of Orbital Angular Momentum Channels for Optical Communication
papers.abs: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing has been limited in practice by the complexity and optical loss of the elements that separate the channels at the receiver side. Here we adopt the azimuthal harmonics of OAM petal patterns as the demultiplexing basis, which makes the receiver the optical counterpart of the circular antenna arrays used in radio OAM links: the petal pattern of topological charge $\ell$ carries a single azimuthal harmonic of order $2\ell$, so one Fourier transform of the azimuthal intensity profile returns every channel, without gratings or mode sorters. The petals are formed by projecting a vector vortex beam from a single q-plate onto a linear polarization. A two-channel system at 515 nm with a 16-position circular photoreceiver array reaches 5.2 Gb/s below the forward error correction threshold, 2.6 Gb/s per channel from a 1.4 GHz photoreceiver.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Beam-Displacement Estimation for Inter-Satellite Quantum-Secure Time Transfer
papers.abs: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. The investigation focuses on a quantum-enhanced scheme in which squeezing is added to the derivative mode of a Gaussian probe beam as a means of estimating photon-beam displacement. The performance of the scheme is compared against the standard quantum limit achieved by an optimal classical beam-displacement estimation scheme under a fair same-total-energy constraint. We find that although the benefit provided by squeezing rapidly diminishes as the inter-satellite distance increases due to diffraction-induced beam spreading and subsequent truncation by the finite receiver aperture, a quantum advantage can still be expected over inter-satellite distances up to approximately 100 km under practical satellite configurations. This distance scale between satellites is anticipated for Starlink-type satellite constellations.

papers.abs: We present the phase diagram of a one-dimensional quantum Rabi zigzag chain under an artificial gauge field, which is implemented via phase-modulated next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping. For strong nearest-neighbor (NN) coupling, the system exhibits either a ferro-superradiant (FSR) or an antiferro-superradiant (AFSR) phase depending on its sign. Increasing NNN coupling induces a stripe antiferro-superradiant (sAFSR) phase with antiparallel NNN and parallel NN displacements, which is distinct from the conventional AFSR phase. Tuning the magnetic flux drives the system into chiral or antichiral superradiant phases with opposite ground-state photon currents, which are different from the conventional superradiant phases. Remarkably, geometric frustration within each triangular plaquette stabilizes chiral phases even at small magnetic flux while suppressing the sAFSR phase, which vanishes for $N=6$. papers.abs: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructure diode. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.

papers.abs: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The method handles entangled bands and accurately reproduces TDDFPT at a fraction of its cost. papers.title: From proof of concept to practice: the next decade of artificial intelligence in metasurface photonics
papers.abs: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence has learned to predict electromagnetic responses rapidly and generate high-performance metasurface designs. However, one question remains open: compared with conventional design workflows that contain no learned model, has it made the complete design workflow faster, and are the resulting devices better? We argue that the answer depends on the task. Reading 100 highly cited optical studies in depth, we distinguish the design tasks in which artificial intelligence is irreplaceable, clearly advantageous, or without clear advantage. In our view, the key to the next decade is not more successes in isolated tasks but making each success a foundation for the field, through shifts such as shared data, trained models, and physics written into learning. Whether artificial intelligence leaves lasting value in this field will depend on whether its benefits can be verified, its methods transferred, and its designs corrected by experiment.

papers.title: Microscopic Theory of Spin-Orbit Interactions of Light
papers.abs: Optical spin-orbit interactions (SOI), demonstrated experimentally in optical cavities, enable the polarization degrees of freedom of light to be described and controlled as an effective pseudospin, providing a foundation for spintronic-like control of light and the development of next-generation optical technologies. However, prior works describe this emergent effect using phenomenological models that fail to uncover its microscopic quantum origins, and as a result, a rigorous connection between material electronic structure and the optical SOI remains elusive. In this work, we address this fundamental challenge by developing a microscopic quantum theory starting from the non-relativistic quantum electrodynamical (QED) description of light-matter interactions. We show that this effect arises from virtual interactions between confined photons and material excitations. papers.title: Temperature Evolution of Magnon-Polarons in the van der Waals Antiferromagnet FePS$_3$
papers.abs: Magnon polarons, hybrid excitations arising from magnon-phonon coupling, were investigated in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using magneto-Raman scattering measurements at temperatures ranging from 4 K to the vicinity of the Néel temperature ($T_\mathrm{N}$ = 118 K). The lower Zeeman-split component of the magnon-like mode, tuned by the magnetic field toward the lower-energy phonon mode, exhibits an avoided crossing. The corresponding magnetic field decreases from approximately 13 T at 4 K to 5.6 T at 85 K, bringing the effect within reach of a standard laboratory magnet. A model of three coupled bosonic modes shows that the magnon-phonon coupling constant, approximately 2.7 cm$^{-1}$ at low temperatures, decreases significantly with increasing temperature, following a trend similar to the temperature-induced softening of the magnon mode. This decrease in magnon-phonon coupling is discussed in terms of a possible reduction in sublattice magnetization due to thermal fluctuations.

papers.title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
papers.abs: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The relative sensitivities achieved for various principal quantum numbers are presented. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.

papers.abs: Sender authentication is an important requirement for secure quantum communication networks. Our scheme relies on a time-resolved coherent detection method introduced here, in which the coherent responses from individual time-bins are sequentially accumulated within Bob's spin coherence prior to the final sender verification. papers.title: Metadevices that compute: mathematical foundations and experimental implementations for neuromorphic nanophotonics
papers.abs: Wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a compelling alternative to digital electronics for specific linear-algebraic and machine-learning workloads, promising massively parallel, high-bandwidth, and energy-efficient information processing. Metamaterials, metasurfaces, and integrated metastructures (collectively, metadevices) now perform mathematical operations, solve integral and differential equations, multiply matrices, and implement trainable photonic neural networks directly in the wave domain. This focused review consolidates the mathematical foundations that underpin such devices, i.e., the mapping between linear operators and wave scattering, the feedback architectures that realize equation inversion, and the inverse-design and scientific machine-learning toolchains that make their synthesis and training tractable, and connects them to the rapidly growing body of experimental demonstrations, from free-space diffractive processors to reconfigurable guided-wave metastructures. papers.abs: In this paper we present a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. papers.abs: Topological photonic structures provide a powerful means of confining and directing light through interface states formed between photonic phases with distinct topological properties. This flexibility allows topological photonic confinement and strong excitonic coupling to be engineered separately within the same structure. Here, patterned low-loss dielectric hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) defines the photonic modes, while an encapsulated WSe2 monolayer provides the excitonic resonance that couples directly to the confined optical field. papers.abs: Interfacing quantum materials with photonic cavity architectures is at the vanguard of materials engineering. The structured electromagnetic fluctuations of a dark cavity environment can renormalize fundamental thermodynamical material properties and energy scales, holding promise to create a rich ecosystem of cavity-induced ground states and functionalities absent in the bare material. However, direct experimental demonstrations that cavity coupling can stabilize or enhance genuinely new phases of matter have remained scarce. In this work, we establish the presence of cavity-induced and cavity-enhanced ferroelectric phases in free-standing SrTiO$_3$ membranes coupled to dark THz-frequency photonic crystal cavities. Using THz spectroscopy, we observe ultrastrong coupling (USC) between the ferroelectric soft mode in SrTiO$_3$ and the cavity resonance. papers.abs: We investigate magnon-photon interactions in a resonant cavity starting from the coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations linearized about an arbitrary micromagnetic ground state. By introducing an electric vector potential and a suitable interaction Lagrangian, the formulation avoids the cancellation of large magnetostatic contributions that arises in the conventional magnetic-vector-potential description and becomes inaccurate under modal truncation. The magnetization and cavity fields are expanded in the normal modes of the uncoupled magnetic and electromagnetic subsystems, with coupling coefficients given by overlap integrals of the corresponding eigenfunctions. The resulting multimode Lagrangian has a noncanonical structure due to the gyrotropic terms, and the corresponding Hamiltonian formulation is obtained using the Faddeev-Jackiw approach. papers.title: Fault-Tolerant Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Metrology with Bosonic Probes
papers.abs: Quantum sensors have been shown to enable more precise measurements than classical sensors. By using entanglement and coherent evolution, the estimation error can be made to scale better in interrogation time, photon count, and other resources, achieving Heisenberg-limited scaling. However, environmental noise and hardware errors typically destroy the coherence of the sensitive quantum states. This motivates the use of fault-tolerant techniques to create more robust quantum sensing protocols. Such fault-tolerant quantum sensing approaches have been shown to enhance sensitivity for qubit systems, but many practical sensors require bosonic probes. In this paper, we propose a fault-tolerant protocol using bosons to estimate displacements in the presence of dephasing noise. We construct an optimal error-correcting code under a mean photon-number constraint. Controlled displacements couple the probe to a repetition-encoded qubit register, while repeated boson-parity measurements and resets remove probe noise without erasing the stored logical phase. papers.title: Characterizing Reaction Types through Linear Free-Energy Relationships in Cavities
papers.abs: Polaritonic chemistry holds the promise of controlling chemical reactivity through confined light-matter interactions, yet how reactions respond inside optical cavities remains debated. Here, we take a more zoomed-out view, inspired by electrostatic catalysis. We extend nonempirical linear free-energy relationships to cavity-modified reactions and show that their behavior falls into four distinct reaction types set by simple response-crossing rules. Reactions can follow conventional Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) or counterintuitive Opposite-BEP behavior regardless of cavity tuning, or switch between the two as the cavity frequency is varied. We establish this picture analytically and demonstrate it in the Shin Metiu model and in four molecular reactions treated with ab initio electronic-structure methods. papers.title: Soliton-Lattice Origin of Incommensurability in High-Pressure Antimony
papers.abs: The microscopic origin of incommensurability in host-guest crystals remains unresolved. Here we show that the high-pressure antimony host-guest phase Sb-II is a soliton lattice, where localized guest-host misregistries decorate a commensurate 4/3 reference structure. First-principles calculations reveal a corrugated and hysteretic registry landscape, motivating a Frenkel-Kontorova description that accounts for soliton-lattice approximants of the form $(4n+1)/(3n+1)$. Machine-learning-potential calculations of these approximants show an energetically preferred soliton spacing, and their localized misregistry cores are also verified by first-principles relaxations. At finite temperature, the thermally broadened soliton lattice appears as an atomic density wave along the guest chains, consistent with experimental diffraction. This soliton-registry picture provides a microscopic mechanism for host-guest incommensurability in Sb-II.

papers.abs: An algebraic correspondence between an imaging model and a quantum state does not specify a computational method: input access, measurement and decoding determine what can be returned. Complex-field interference motivates unknown-phase inference: complementary measurements resolve ambiguities that local Fisher information alone does not detect. papers.abs: Neutral atoms in optical tweezer arrays have emerged as a leading platform for quantum information processing. The fidelity of entangling gates mediated by Rydberg interactions has improved rapidly and is increasingly constrained by blackbody-radiation-induced transitions, which shorten Rydberg lifetimes and create contaminant states that can cause correlated errors. Cryogenic environments can suppress these transition rates by more than an order of magnitude. However, realizing a universal gate set in such an environment has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate a universal quantum gate set in a cryogenic $^{133}$Cs atom array, with a single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.970(2)% and a raw two-qubit entangling-gate fidelity of 99.76(8)%, within the range of leading room-temperature implementations. The entangling gate uses direct single-photon coupling between the electronic ground state and a Rydberg $P$ state, avoiding scattering and light shifts associated with two-photon coupling. papers.abs: Cavity-enhanced spectroscopy is a widely used experimental technique. papers.abs: Sommerfeld's half-plane problem, describing diffraction of a monochromatic wave by a semi-infinite perfectly electric conducting (PEC) infinitesimally thin plate, is one of the cornerstones of classical electromagnetic scattering theory. Unlike the PEC plate, the Drude medium supports evanescent penetration of the field prior to its temporal transition; the temporal interface here acts as the analogue of the sharp spatial boundary in the Sommerfeld problem, but now separates two time intervals rather than two spatial half-planes. papers.abs: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. papers.abs: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers information-theoretic security, but device imperfections introduce implementation vulnerabilities. Receiver measurements confirm that the resulting calibration mismatch leads to overestimated channel transmittance and underestimated excess noise. papers.abs: Spatial wave localization at boundaries is conventionally restricted to exponential decay. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. papers.title: Edge intelligence for distributed acoustic sensing with ultracompact neural networks
papers.abs: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) transforms optical fibres into dense arrays of vibration sensors for continuous, long-range monitoring with high spatial resolution. Existing artificial-intelligence approaches are typically optimized for specific sensing environments and tasks, but their computational requirements can hinder deployment in compact, power-constrained field systems. Here, we introduce DAS-NanoNet, a framework that automatically constructs lightweight neural networks for different DAS scenarios and tasks, together with OmniDAS, an open benchmark spanning six representative environments. Using lightweight temporal operators tailored to DAS signals, an adaptive neural architecture search strategy derives a compact network for each scenario-task pairing.
